summary: Foundation tests meaningfully cover configuration validation, secret redaction, SQLite schema constraints/idempotency, scheduler constants, storage path policy, and boundary behavior without production secrets or network access. One low-severity smoke assertion is weak but does not reduce confidence in the foundation because surrounding tests cover actual behavior.

findings.issue: test_pytest_smoke asserts only that PROJECT_ROOT exists. This proves pytest can execute a test, but it does not protect project behavior beyond what pytest execution itself already proves.
findings.impact: Low. Other tests cover package imports, metadata, config, schema, scheduler, storage, and boundaries, so this is not a blocker.
findings.recommendation: In a future cleanup, replace this with a stronger smoke assertion such as reading pyproject pytest config or importing a second package module.

coverageAssessment.evidence: Tests cover fake env loading, missing required settings, all three Telegram tokens, .env loading, timezone exclusion, and redacted logging.
Tests cover required tables, absence of business-primary tables, idempotent init, draft owner invariant, scheduler/reminder idempotency, and lookup indexes.
Tests cover fixed timezone, env non-override, end date, summary window, reminder times, idempotency keys, audio/PDF/backup paths, and local-only path assertions.
Tests cover fake Sheets without credentials, distinct bot purposes, technical error isolation, operational notification routing, report/speech importability, and forbidden live SDK imports.

taskRequired.reason: Only one low-severity test quality issue was found; no high or critical coverage gaps.
